opening.headline: Learn how to choose the right delivery method and limits when inserting non-textual input into your model, such as a photo of a receipt or a 100-page PDF.
body: Let's say you're building an app that needs to extract the amount and date from a photo of a receipt, or find clauses in a 100-page contract PDF. If you only read text, you may miss tables, stamps, and scanned text. Conversely, if you push a file without knowing the input method and limits, the request may be rejected or the cost may be higher than necessary.

In this class, we compare the same framework of how Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini receive images, and look at how PDF support and the Files API handle request size and page limits. Next, we organize the limits and uses for each delivery method in a table, and explain the process of selecting an input method using a receipt image and a 100-page PDF as an example.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain image understanding, PDF support, delivery method for file upload, and limits for each input method.
You can choose the appropriate delivery method depending on the size of the input and whether it can be reused.

screens.title: I want to extract information from scanned PDFs and images.
screens.lead: Please read the two requirements first. Read while thinking about how the two inputs are different and what would be difficult.

visual.alt: A two-pronged scene where a photo of a receipt and a multi-page PDF document are modeled.
labels: One receipt: extract amount and date
What are the input methods and limits?

paragraphs: There are two requirements: One is to extract the amount and date from a photo of a receipt, and the other is to find a specific clause in a 100-page contract PDF. Both inputs are not data consisting of only letters.

Reading text alone cannot handle this type of input properly. Receipts are photos, so the text must be read from the image, and contracts may contain a mixture of tickets, stamps, and scanned text. The model must be able to directly see the visual elements of images and documents.

Another issue is the input method and limits. There are limits to the size of an image, the number of images you can include in a request, and the number of pages in a PDF. If you don't know the limit, your request will be rejected, and if you choose the wrong method, sending the same file repeatedly will increase costs.

callout.label: question of the day
callout.text: When inserting images and PDFs into a model, which delivery method should you choose and what limits should you check first?

screens.outro: First, let's recall our experience considering resolution when inserting an image into a model.

screens.title: Have you ever considered image resolution?
screens.lead: Have you ever considered resolution when putting images into your model? When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think about it in your head first and then press it.

items.prompt: Will text be readable in an image that is too small?
items.answer: If the resolution is too low, text that is blurry to the human eye will not be readable to the model. In particular, for input that is dense with small letters, such as receipts, the original must be sufficiently clear. Accuracy depends as much on input quality as on model performance.

items.prompt: Wouldn't an image that's too large increase the cost?
items.answer: Images are billed as tokens, so larger sizes require more input tokens. Each model has a maximum resolution it can process, so images larger than that may be reduced before processing. Therefore, sending images larger than necessary only increases costs and delays.

items.prompt: What happens when the number of pages in a PDF increases?
items.answer: As the number of pages increases, the number of input tokens increases and the request size and page limit are approached. This is because text and images are processed together on each page. In the following screen, you will see why it is burdensome to send the entire 100-page PDF for each question.

screens.outro: Now that I have some experience in mind, let's first compare the way the three providers receive images in the same framework.

screens.title: Image understanding: 3rd party input method
screens.lead: Select each tab to compare how the three providers receive images, in order of delivery method, limits, and things to keep in mind.

visual.alt: Illustration showing the three paths an image can take to the model.
labels: File ID (uploaded once and referenced multiple times)

tabs.label: Claude
tabs.body:
**Delivery Method**: Images are base64 encoded and placed directly in the request, pointed to as a URL, or referenced as `file_id` returned by the Files API. For images to be used multiple times, upload them once and reference them as `file_id` to avoid encoding and retransmission.

**Limit**: Images per request: 100 for Context Window 200,000 Token models and 600 for other models. The maximum size of one image is 8000x8000 px. If there are more than 20 images in a request, stricter size limits apply to all images.

**Caution**: When inserting multiple images, separate them by placing a short text label in front of each image, such as Image 1:.

tabs.label: OpenAI
tabs.body:
**Delivery Method**: Provided as a complete URL pointing to the image, a base64 data URL, or a file ID created with the Files API. You can also put multiple images into the `content` array in one request.

**Limits and Fees**: Images are calculated and charged as tokens. The image preprocessing level is determined by the `detail` parameter. The values ​​are `low`, `high`, `original`, `auto`, or if omitted, it is `auto`. If detailed visual information is required, such as character recognition, use `original` if supported.

**Note**: `low` does not always spend less tokens than `high`.

tabs.label: Gemini
tabs.body:
**Delivery Method**: There are three. Pass public images by URL, send a base64 encoded image inline, or reference a file uploaded using the File API.

**Recommended**: File API uploads are recommended for large files or when reusing the same image across multiple requests. For small images that are only written once, inline is sufficient.

**Note**: All input to the Gemini API is processed as a token. Images are no exception; the more images there are, the more input tokens there are.

screens.outro: Now that we've confirmed the image input, let's look at how to receive a PDF and the Files API.

screens.title: PDF support and Files API
screens.lead: The following steps illustrate the three paths and limits for putting a PDF in a request. Select the right arrow to go through the steps one by one.

visual.alt: An illustration comparing the path for sending a PDF inline and the path for uploading it to the Files API and referencing it by file_id.

steps.title: What you can read in PDF
steps.body: Claude's PDF support reads not only text, but also pictures, charts, and tables. All active models support PDF processing. Gemini also understands the context of the entire document with native vision to analyze text, images, diagrams, charts, and tables, and handles documents up to 1,000 pages long.

steps.title: Claude's PDF Limits
steps.body: The maximum request size is 32MB, and the maximum page count is 600 pages per request. If the request's context window is less than 1 million tokens, the page limit is 100 pages. This limit is based on the total request size, including not just the PDF but any other content sent along with it.

steps.title: Send inline
steps.body: This method encodes the PDF in base64 and inserts it directly into the request. The Gemini documentation explains that this method is suitable for small documents or temporary processing. This is simple when you don't want to refer to the same file again in subsequent requests.

steps.title: Upload to Files API
steps.body: There is a way to upload a large PDF once using the Files API and refer to it using the returned `file_id`. The request does not include a file body, resulting in a smaller request size. This is especially useful if you ask multiple questions on the same PDF. Gemini also recommends Inline for small documents and Files API for large documents.

steps.title: file management
steps.body: Claude's Files API allows you to list uploaded files, get metadata, and delete them. List inquiries are responded to page by page, with a default of 20 and a maximum of 1,000. Delete and organize files that are no longer used.

steps.title: Non-PDF documents
steps.body: You can deliver non-PDF documents in the same way in Gemini, but they appear as plain text and lose context like charts and formatting. Documents with important tables and charts should be exported as PDF to take advantage of visual elements.

data.notes: As the number of pages and resolution increases, the number of input tokens increases, increasing cost and delay. Claude divides the image into 28x28 pixel pieces and counts each piece as one visual token. Each model has a maximum resolution it can process, and images exceeding this are reduced before processing. Therefore, sending an image larger than necessary may only increase costs and delays without increasing accuracy. Remember, as shown in the last row of the table, limits apply based on the entire request, not just the single file you send.

screens.outro: Now that we have organized it into a table, let us explain the process of applying it to two cases.

screens.title: Case Commentary: Receipt Images
screens.lead: The instructor explains step by step the process of extracting the amount and date from a photo of a receipt. Select the right arrow to follow from selecting an input method to determining confidence.

visual.alt: A scene from a receipt image with the amount and date areas highlighted and the extracted fields shown next to them.

steps.title: Decide on the input method
steps.body: The input is one image and we only use it once. If the image is not already hosted, add it directly to the request as base64, or pass it as a URL if there is a public address. You don't need the Files API since you won't reuse it.

steps.title: Step 1: Make sure the text is at a readable resolution
steps.body: For images with a lot of small text, such as receipts, the text will be blurry if the resolution is low. First, check whether the amount and date are clearly legible to the human eye in the original. An image that cannot be read cannot be read by the model.

steps.title: Step 2: Reduce images that are too large
steps.body: If the image is larger than the model's maximum resolution, it is reduced before processing. If you send the size as is, which will be reduced anyway, transmission and costs will only increase. Reduce input tokens by lowering the resolution to a range where the required characters are readable.

steps.title: Step 3: Structure your request with the required fields
steps.body: Decide in advance the fields to be selected, such as date and amount, and ask them to be presented in a structured format. You can then use the results directly in your code. The question clearly states the scope of finding only the date and total amount on the receipt.

steps.title: Step 4: Don’t trust the blurry parts
steps.body: Because the text is blurred, we do not trust the values that the model may have guessed. In this case, leave a path to guide the user to retake the shot. The service flow reflects that image understanding depends on input quality.

screens.outro: This time, we will look at an example of a 100-page PDF with the exact opposite input method.

screens.title: Case Commentary: 100-page PDF
screens.lead: The instructor explains the process of finding clauses in a 100-page contract. Select the arrow to the right to follow along from checking your limits to choosing a processing method.

steps.title: Upload once via Files API
steps.body: Since I'm asking the same contract multiple times, I upload it once to the Files API and reference it repeatedly as `file_id`. Sending inline would result in 100 pages per question in the request, increasing the size and cost.

steps.title: First check if the page count is within the limit.
steps.body: Claude's page limit is 100 pages if the context window is less than 1 million tokens, and 600 pages if it is more. 100 pages is right on the border of your limit, so check the window size of the model you're using first. Also see the 32MB request size limit.

steps.title: Divide only the necessary sections
steps.body: If the question is about a specific chapter, shorten the input tokens by including only that section. Costs and delays are reduced rather than sending the whole thing every time, and you can focus on what you need the model for.

steps.title: If there are tables and charts, it can be based on vision.
steps.body: If your contract contains tables and charts, use PDF processing to read the visuals rather than just the text. Converting to just plain text loses the context of your charts and formatting.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed the two cases, I will conclude by summarizing the key points.

screens.title: Key points and reflection
screens.lead: Review the key points of this lesson on one screen. Read the paragraph below and proceed to the summary screen.

paragraphs: The form of input changes cost and accuracy. Images are sent as base64, URL, and file ID, and PDFs are uploaded to the Files API if they are large or repeatedly used within the limit.

Resolution and page count affect input tokens and accuracy. Before sending the input, check the limits for size, pages, and number of images, and determine the delivery method based on whether or not it will be reused.

glossary.def: This is a function where the model reads letters, objects, and structures in an image and answers questions.
This is a function that reads and understands the text of a document and visual elements such as pictures, charts, and tables together.
This is an API that uploads a file once and references it in multiple requests using the returned file_id.
Limitations set by the delivery method, such as request size, number of pages, number of images, and image resolution.

misconceptions.fact: Claude and Gemini read PDF text as well as visual elements such as pictures, charts, and tables. Non-PDF documents appear as plain text, losing visual context.

misconceptions.myth: The larger the image, the more accurate it is.
misconceptions.fact: Each model has a maximum resolution it can process, and images larger than that are reduced. As size increases, input tokens and delays also increase, so an appropriate resolution is required for the text to be readable.

misconceptions.myth: The limits are the same for all providers.
misconceptions.fact: Image count, page count, and request size limits vary by provider and model. For example, Claude's page limit is 100 or 600 pages, depending on the context window size, while the Gemini document guides for a maximum of 1000 pages.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: The type of input changes cost and accuracy.
For images and PDFs, check the delivery method and limits first.
Files to be reused are uploaded and referenced using the Files API.
Resolution and page count affect input tokens and accuracy.
